**Commentary**

Occupancy remains high, which tells us that capacity is well used and that scheduling of elective admissions needs constant attention. The outpatient figure in the table shows a very busy clinic network feeding the wards, and the surgical volume reflects a steady operating theatre schedule.

For context, our sister hospital, Sister Jyoion Hospital, operates 350 beds. In FY22 it admitted 68,743 inpatients and earned Rs 0.746 billion from inpatient services. These are Sister Jyoion Hospital's numbers only and should not be added to ours.

Turning to inpatient care at Versha Multispeciality Hospital, admissions averaged 4,207 per month across the whole of FY22. Inpatient revenue grew from Rs. 802 million in FY21 to ₹10,063 lakh in FY22, a rise that reflects both heavier ward use and a richer case mix.

We will keep reporting these indicators each year so that clinicians, trustees and referring doctors can follow how the hospital is changing.

**Vasvat Agro Producer Cooperative: Rabi 2026 Chana Season Review**

Summary: Vasvat Agro Producer Cooperative in Hisar district, registered in 2014, ended the rabi 2026 season with a respectable realisation but a heavier cost burden than its neighbour. Costs and prices tell most of the story.

Costs and prices

- Average cultivation cost, covering seed, fertiliser, labour and irrigation, was twenty-four thousand three hundred rupees per acre.
- The cooperative realised an average of Rs. 5,975 per quintal on its chana, while the mandi modal price at harvest, a separate market benchmark, averaged ₹6,130 per quintal. The government MSP was ₹5,440 per quintal.

Neighbour comparison

- Arkavista FPO realised an average of Rs. 6,235 per quintal in the same season.
- Arkavista FPO's cultivation cost was Rs 17,750 per acre, clearly lower.
- Arkavista FPO's average yield was 9 quintals per acre.

Yield and area

- Vasvat's average chana yield was 6.2 quintals per acre.
- Members cultivated 12,945 acres of chana.
- Rainfall during the season was 368 mm.
- Warehouse capacity stands at 6,100 tonnes.

Risks: Higher input costs and a yield gap with neighbouring cooperatives could erode margins, and a mandi price above the realised price suggests the cooperative may be selling too early.

**Triora Healthcare: Extract from the Management Discussion**

Triora Healthcare, the hospital in Lucknow operated under the trust, completed fiscal 2025 with its facilities fully functional across a capacity of 540 beds. The Board records its appreciation of the clinical and administrative staff who sustained services throughout the year.

Total patient revenue for fiscal 2025 was Rs 3014.56 cr. Inpatient services contributed fifty-two per cent of that total. In the same period, pharmacy and ancillary income, which is a separate stream and is not counted within patient revenue, amounted to two hundred and thirty-four crore rupees. A year earlier, inpatient revenue had been Rs 12.382 billion, and the Board notes the continued strengthening of this segment against the previous year.

On activity levels, the hospital recorded 8,24,700 outpatient visits and consultations. Inpatient admissions averaged 5,206 per month across the whole of fiscal 2025, reflecting steady demand for admitted care.

The state government released a grant of Rs 283.6 crore towards the construction of a new cardiac wing. This grant is a capital contribution and has not been included in patient revenue. The Board expresses its gratitude to the government for its support and expects the wing to widen the range of cardiac services available to patients in the region.

The Board will continue to review clinical quality, patient safety and financial prudence in the coming year.

**Shridhi Ltd: a Kolkata IT services business in profile**

**Summary.** Shridhi Ltd, founded in 2000 and based in Kolkata, builds software and handles cloud migration for clients. It runs across 17 offices and employs 7,140 people. Over the years under review its top line has climbed steadily, though margins stayed thin, and in one year the business slipped into a small operating loss.

**Key points**

- Starting point: revenue in 2018-19 was Rs. 529 million.
- The business reached the next stage in 2019-20, when revenue moved from Rs. 529 million earlier to ₹0.64 billion while operating expenses in 2019-20 were ₹58.9 crore, all captured here in one line: revenue was ₹0.64 billion and operating expenses were ₹58.9 crore in 2019-20.

**Survista Multispeciality Hospital Releases Annual Report, Showing Strong Clinical and Financial Year**

FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE

Chennai: Survista Multispeciality Hospital has published its annual report for FY21, describing a year of steady clinical growth and sound finances.

The hospital operates 670 beds and is supported by a medical staff of 80 doctors. Running the institution is a significant undertaking: total operating expenses for FY21, covering the hospital's running costs, came to Rs 1,70,230 lakh. After all costs, the hospital recorded a net surplus of Rs. 354.9 crore.

On the revenue side, total patient revenue for FY21 was ₹2404.91 crore. Inpatient services contributed 55 per cent of that total, confirming the central role of acute and surgical care in the hospital's mix.

The activity behind those results is visible in admissions, which rose from 65,050 in the year before to 76,047 in FY21.

"Our teams worked relentlessly to meet rising demand, and these results belong to every doctor, nurse and technician who made it possible," said the hospital's chief administrator. "We will keep reinvesting in people and equipment."

The report also highlights quality initiatives and patient-experience programmes, which the hospital says will remain priorities.

**Verora Farmers Producer Company: rabi 2022 season report, interview**

Q: How did the mustard crop go for your members?

A: Verora Farmers Producer Company has 2,151 member farmers, and together they grew mustard on 10,530 acres in the rabi 2022 season. Total production was 92,664 quintals.

Q: How did prices compare?

A: Prices ran well above policy support. The government minimum support price was ₹5,650 per quintal, our average realised price was ₹6,825 per quintal, and the open-market mandi modal price at harvest, a different price from what we realised, was Rs. 7,285 per quintal.

Q: What about costs?

A: Cultivation cost averaged ₹20,000 per acre, covering seed, fertiliser, labour and irrigation. Separately, we received a drip irrigation subsidy of ₹22.5 lakh, which is not part of cultivation cost.

Q: Any infrastructure to mention?

A: Our warehouse holds 4,900 tonnes, which let us time sales rather than rush produce to the mandi at harvest.

Total cultivation cost for all members together, covering seed, fertiliser, labour and irrigation, was ₹20.9016 crore. Separately, the cooperative received a subsidy of Rs 46.3 lakh for drip irrigation equipment, which is not a cultivation cost. Rainfall during the season was 1,045 mm.

"Our members worked hard and the realised price stayed well above what the open market offered at harvest," said the chairperson of the cooperative. "We will keep investing in better irrigation and fair marketing."
